extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users and developers; computational number theorists using the PARI library
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions (mostly number-theory and finite-field routines), describing semantics, parameters, return values, examples, algorithmic notes, flags and warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor polynomials/integers: irreducible factors are returned sorted by increasing degree. Use factor(GEN x) or boundfact(GEN x, ulong lim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gp_factor0(GEN x, GEN lim = NULL). Note: obsolete GEN factor0(GEN x, long lim) kept for backward compatibility. Use gp interface only for gp_factor0. See nffactor for other factorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorback
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives back the factored object corresponding to a factorization. Integer 1 corresponds to the empty factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If e present, e and f must be vectors of same length and returns product of f[i]^e[i]. If e omitted and f is a vector, treat e as vector of 1s. f may also be a regular factorization as produced by factor commands. Examples: factor(12) -> [2 2; 3 1]; factorback(%) -> 12; factorback([2,3],[2,1]) -> 12. Library: GEN factorback2(GEN f, GEN e = NULL) or GEN factorback(GEN f) (e = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorcantor
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x modulo prime p using distinct-degree plus Cantor–Zassenhaus; coefficients must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns two-column matrix: irreducible polynomials and exponents. For only degrees use factormod(x,p,1). factormod may be faster. Library: GEN factcantor(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorff
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x in the finite field F_q defined by irreducible polynomial a over F_p. Coefficients must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns two-column matrix: irreducible factors and exponents. If all coefficients of x are in Fp a faster algorithm using exponents is applied. Either a or p can be omitted if x has t_FFELT coefficients; then identical to factor. Examples show syntax and common errors (need a t_FFELT coefficient). Library: GEN factorff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial / mpfact / mpfactr
rubrics_metrics.description: factorial(x): returns a real number for x!; expression x! gives integer. mpfact returns x! as a t_INT. mpfactr computes with precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN mpfactr(long x, long prec). GEN mpfact(long x) returns integer factorial. Note distinction between operator x! and function factorial(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors integer n into product of pseudoprimes using a combination of SQUFOF, Pollard Rho, Lenstra ECM, MPQS and pure-power search; output is two-column matrix like factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By convention 0 -> 0^1, 1 -> empty factorization. Divisors > 2^64 are by default not proven prime (only failed BPSW); use isprime or set factor_proven default to 1 to guarantee primality. Private prime tables entries included. flag is optional; binary digits: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first-stage ECM, 4 avoid Rho and SQUFOF, 8 don't run final ECM. Note algorithm is probabilistic; composites might not be detected though no example is known. Use gp debug levels to observe internals. Library: GEN factorint(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormod
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x modulo prime p using Berlekamp; coefficients must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns two-column matrix: irreducible polynomials and exponents. If flag non-zero, outputs only degrees of irreducible polynomials (useful for L-function computation). factorcantor is an alternative algorithm sometimes faster. Library: GEN factormod0(GEN x, GEN p, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffgen
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a t_FFELT generator for finite field with q elements (q = p^f prime power). Computes an irreducible monic polynomial P ∈ Fp[X] of degree f via ffinit and returns g = X mod P(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If v given, variable name used to display g. Alternative: input monic irreducible polynomial P directly to infer p. Warning: if P not irreducible, result is invalid and behavior undefined; testing P for irreducibility is more costly than producing it via ffinit. Library: GEN ffgen(GEN q, long v = -1). To create generator for prime field: GEN p_to_GEN(GEN p, long v) returns 1+ffgen(x*Mod(1,p),v). Examples and error message for non-prime q (e.g., ffgen(6) errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffinit
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a monic irreducible polynomial of degree n over Fp (p prime) using fast Adleman–Lenstra variant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful with ffgen: P = ffinit(3,2) etc. Library: GEN ffinit(GEN p, long n, long v = -1) where v is variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: fflog
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete logarithm of finite field element x in base g: returns e in Z with g^e = x. If o provided, o represents multiplicative order of g (preferred format [ord, factor(ord)]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no o given assume g primitive. Result undefined if e does not exist. Algorithms used: combination of generic discrete-log algorithms (see znlog), cubic-sieve index-calculus for large fields degree ≥5, Coppersmith's algorithm for characteristic ≤5. Library: GEN fflog(GEN x, GEN g, GEN o = NULL). Examples and usage with ffprimroot to obtain o and primitive roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffnbirred
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes number of monic irreducible polynomials over Fq of degree exactly n (flag=0) or at most n (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN ffnbirred0(GEN q, long n, long fl). Also GEN ffnbirred(GEN q, long n) and GEN ffsumnbirred(GEN q, long n) for flag variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: fforder
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplicative order of finite-field element x. If o present it represents a multiple of the order (preferred [N, factor(N)] where N is cardinality of multiplicative group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing o can be much faster. Examples show timing with and without o. Library: GEN fforder(GEN x, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffprimroot
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a primitive root of the multiplicative group of the definition field of finite-field element x. If &o present, o is set to [ord, fa] where ord is order and fa its factorization factor(ord).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: o is useful for fflog and fforder. Library: GEN ffprimroot(GEN x, GEN *o = NULL). Examples show resulting ord and factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: fibonacci
rubrics_metrics.description: xth Fibonacci number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN fibo(long x).

rubrics_metrics.name: gcd
rubrics_metrics.description: Greatest common divisor of x and y. If y omitted and x is a vector, returns gcd of all components (equivalent to content(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x and y can be many types (e.g., rationals). For x,y where one is vector/matrix, gcd applied recursively producing result of same type as vector/matrix. Note gcd not commutative for vector/matrix types. Algorithms: naive Euclid except for special inputs: integers use modified right-shift binary algorithm; univariate polynomials with coeffs in same number field use modular gcd; general polynomials use subresultant when coefficient explosion likely. For inexact polynomial coefficients, gcd defined to be scalar; use polresultant to check closeness to non-trivial gcd and gcdext to compute approximate gcd and cofactors. Library: GEN ggcd0(GEN x, GEN y = NULL); other aliases GEN ggcd, GEN content.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcdext
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns [u, v, d] such that d = gcd(x,y) and x*u + y*v = d, with u and v minimal in natural sense. Arguments must be integers or polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: gcdext(32,102) -> [16,-5,2]. For polynomials with inexact coefficients, computes u,v,d with d approximately dividing both; output not mathematically well-defined but provides explicit polynomials to check approximation. Library: GEN gcdext0(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilbert symbol of x and y modulo prime p, p=0 meaning place at infinity (result undefined if p != 0 is not prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit p: take p=0 if both x and y rational or one real; take p=q if one of x,y is t_INTMOD modulo q or a q-adic. Incompatible types raise error. Library: long hilbert(GEN x, GEN y, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: isfundamental
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x equals 1 or the discriminant of a quadratic field, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: long isfundamental(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispolygonal
rubrics_metrics.description: True if integer x is an s-gonal number, false otherwise. Parameter s > 2 must be t_INT. If &N provided set N to index n (n-th s-gonal number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ispolygonal(36,3,&N) returns 1 and sets N. Library: long ispolygonal(GEN x, GEN s, GEN *N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispower
rubrics_metrics.description: If k given, returns true if x is a k-th power. If k omitted (integers/fractions only), returns maximal k ≥ 2 such that x = n^k or 0 if none. For t_FFELT x, k omitted not allowed; use formula k = (x.p^poldegree(x.pol)-1)/fforder(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third argument &n if given sets n to a k-th root when applicable. Library: long ispower(GEN x, GEN k = NULL, GEN *n = NULL). Also long gisanypower(GEN x, GEN *pty) when k omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ispowerful
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is a powerful integer (valuation at all primes > 1), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ispowerful(50) -> 0, ispowerful(100) -> 1. Library: long ispowerful(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: isprime
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is a prime number, false (0) otherwise. Routine proves/disproves rigorously but can be slow for large primes (e.g., >1000 digits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts vectors/matrices componentwise. flag=0 uses combination of Baillie-PSW, Selfridge p-1 test (if x-1 smooth), and APRCL for general x. flag=1 uses Selfridge-Pocklington-Lehmer p-1 test and outputs a primality certificate: returns 0 (composite), 1 (small enough that passing BPSW guarantees primality, currently x < 2^64), 2 (large prime proven only using APRCL), or a three-column matrix as certificate when x large and x-1 smooth. Algorithm may fail if pseudo-prime factors not prime (exceedingly unlikely). Debug levels may show warnings about untested integers being declared primes due to partial factorizations. flag=2 uses APRCL. Library: GEN gisprime(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimepower
rubrics_metrics.description: If x = p^k with p prime and k>0 return k, else 0. If &n provided and x a prime power, set n to p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: long isprimepower(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispseudoprime
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is a strong pseudoprime (highly likely prime), false otherwise. If false then x not prime; if true use isprime to prove primality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts vectors/matrices componentwise. flag=0 checks Baillie-Pomerance-Selfridge-Wagstaff pseudoprime (strong Rabin–Miller base 2 followed by strong Lucas test). No known composites pass this test (though expected infinitely many may exist); all composites ≤ 2^64 are correctly detected. flag>0 uses strong Miller–Rabin for flag random bases. Library: GEN gispseudoprime(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: issquare
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is a square, false otherwise. Meaning depends on type: all complex numbers are squares; non-negative reals are squares; exact types (INT, FRAC, INTMOD) squares are s^2 with s in Z,Q,Z/NZ respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If &n given, put a square root into n. Examples: issquare(3)->0, issquare(3.)->1, issquare(Mod(7,8))->0, issquare(4,&n) sets n=2. For polynomials, detect characteristic 2 or assume 2 invertible and check via truncated power series. Library: long issquareall(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL) and long issquare(GEN x). Deprecated GP-specific functions gissquare return gen 0/1 instead of boolean.

rubrics_metrics.name: issquarefree
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is squarefree, false otherwise. x can be integer or polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: long issquarefree(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: istotient
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x = φ(n) for some integer n, false otherwise. If &N given set N to such n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: istotient(14)->0, istotient(4, &n) returns 1 and sets n=10. Library: long istotient(GEN x, GEN *N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: kronecker
rubrics_metrics.description: Kronecker symbol (x|y) for integers x and y: total multiplicativity with special rules for y=0,-1,2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules: (x|0)=1 if |x|=1 else 0; (x|-1)=1 if x≥0 else -1; (x|2)=0 if x even, 1 if x=1 or x≡±1 mod 8, -1 if x≡±3 mod 8. Library: long kronecker(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: lcm
rubrics_metrics.description: Least common multiple of x and y, satisfying lcm(x,y)*gcd(x,y)=abs(x*y). If y omitted and x is vector, returns lcm of components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When one argument is vector/matrix, LCM taken recursively; result has same type as the vector/matrix and is not necessarily commutative. Note lcm(v) differs from iterative loop and uses divide-and-conquer tree for efficiency, especially with GMP kernel. Example timings provided. Library: GEN glcm0(GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: logint
rubrics_metrics.description: Return largest integer e such that b^e ≤ x for integers b>1 and x>0. If &z present set it to b^e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: logint(1000,2) -> 9 and z=512. Useful to compute number of digits: #digits(1000!,10)=1+logint(1000!,10). Replaces floor(log(x)/log(b)) which may be incorrect due to rounding. Library: long logint0(GEN x, GEN b, GEN *z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: moebius
rubrics_metrics.description: Moebius µ-function of |x|. x must be integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: long moebius(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nextprime
rubrics_metrics.description: Find the smallest pseudoprime ≥ x. x can be any real type. If x is pseudoprime returns x (not strictly larger). To rigorously prove primality use isprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN nextprime(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numbpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of unrestricted partitions p(n) (number of nonnegative integer solutions to a+2b+3c+...=n). n must be integer and n<10^15, with p(n)=0 for n<0 and p(0)=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm uses Hardy–Ramanujan–Rademacher formula. To enumerate partitions use partitions function. Library: GEN numbpart(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: numdiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of divisors of |x|. x must be integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN numdiv(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: omega / bigomega
rubrics_metrics.description: omega(x): number of distinct prime divisors of |x| (without multiplicity). bigomega(x): counts with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: factor(392) shows [2^3,7^2]; omega(392)=2; bigomega(392)=5. Library: long omega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of partitions of integer k as sum of positive integers; partition represented as t_VECSMALL with parts sorted nondecreasing. For k<0 returns empty set, k=0 returns trivial partition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters n (length restrictions) and a (part size restrictions): n=nmax or [nmin,nmax]; a=amax or [amin,amax]. By default parts positive and zero entries removed unless amin ≤ 0, in which case nmin ignored and X is constant length nmax. Examples illustrate partitions(3), partitions(4,2) (parts bounded by 2), partitions(4,,2) (at most 2 parts), partitions(4,[0,3]) (parts between 0 and3 leading to fixed-length vectors). Library: GEN partitions(long k, GEN a = NULL, GEN n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsff
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns vector of distinct roots of polynomial x in field F_q defined by irreducible polynomial a over F_p. Coefficients must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. a or p can be omitted if x has t_FFELT coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show syntax and errors when base field not determined; prefer second syntax with explicit generator for readability. Library: GEN polrootsff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: precprime
rubrics_metrics.description: Find the largest pseudoprime ≤ x. x any real type. Returns 0 if x ≤ 1. If x is prime returns x (not strictly smaller). To rigorously prove primality use isprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN precprime(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: prime
rubrics_metrics.description: The nth prime number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prime(10^9) = 22801763489. Uses checkpointing and a naive O(n) algorithm. Library: GEN prime(long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: primepi
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime counting function: number of primes p ≤ x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and note: uses checkpointing and naive O(x) algorithm. Library: GEN primepi(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates row vector of first n primes. A t_VEC n = [a,b] is allowed, returning primes in [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns empty vector for n ≤ 0. Examples: primes(10) -> first 10 primes; primes([0,29]) primes up to29; primes([15,30]) returns primes between 15 and30. Library: GEN primes0(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbclassno
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary class number of quadratic order of discriminant D. Uses O(D^{1/2}) algorithm for D>0 and Shanks O(|D|^{1/4}) for D<0. D should not be too large for reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=1 computes class number using Euler products and functional equation in O(|D|^{1/2}). Warning: for D<0 may give incorrect results when class group has many cyclic factors; recommended to double-check with flag=1 or quadclassunit. Warning: routine does not compute number of classes of binary primitive forms (narrow class number) — to get that use QFBclassno(D) = qfbclassno(D) * if (D<0 || norm(quadunit(D))<0,1,2). Examples and library syntax: GEN qfbclassno0(GEN D, long flag) with aliases GEN classno(GEN D) (flag=0) and GEN classno2(GEN D) (flag=1). GEN hclassno(GEN D) computes class number of imaginary quadratic by counting reduced forms in O(|D|).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbcompraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of binary quadratic forms x and y without reduction of result. Useful to compute generating element of an ideal. Result undefined if x and y do not have same discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN qfbcompraw(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbhclassno
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurwitz class number of x, where x non-negative and congruent to 0 or 3 modulo 4. For x > 5·10^5 assumes GRH and uses quadclassunit with default parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN hclassno(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnucomp
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms x and y (type t_QFI) using NUCOMP and NUDUPL algorithms of Shanks (a la Atkin). L is positive constant; for optimal speed take L = |D|^{1/4} where D common discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result undefined if discriminants differ. Current implementation may be slower than generic routine. Library: GEN nucomp(GEN x, GEN y, GEN L); GEN nudupl(GEN x, GEN L) available when x=y.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnupow
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of primitive positive definite binary quadratic form x using Shanks's NUCOMP and NUDUPL algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See qfbnucomp for caveats. Library: GEN nupow(GEN x, GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbpowraw
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of binary quadratic form x computed without reduction (using qfbcompraw). n must be non-negative and < 2^31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN qfbpowraw(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbprimeform
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime binary quadratic form of discriminant x whose first coefficient is p, where |p| is prime. p = ±1 returns unit form. Errors if x not quadratic residue mod p or if x<0 and p<0. Negative definite t_QFI not implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For x>0 the distance component of the form is set to zero according to current precision. Library: GEN primeform(GEN x, GEN p, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbred
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce binary quadratic form x (updating Shanks's distance if x indeﬁnite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag bits: 1 perform single reduction step; 2 don't update Shanks's distance. Optional arguments d, isd, sd supply discriminant and square-root related values (no checking done). If d<0 these values are useless. Library: GEN qfbred0(GEN x, long flag, GEN d = NULL, GEN isd = NULL, GEN sd = NULL). Also available: GEN redimag(GEN x) (for definite x) and for indefinite forms GEN redreal, GEN rhoreal(=qfbred(x,1)), GEN redrealnod(=qfbred(x,2,,isd)), GEN rhorealnod(=qfbred(x,3,,isd)).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbsolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve Q(x,y)=p over integers where Q is binary quadratic form and p a prime. Returns [x,y] as two-component vector or zero if none. Returns only one solution, not all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let D=disc Q. Algorithm runs in probabilistic polynomial time in p; polynomial time in D if Q imaginary, exponential if Q real (requires full cycle of reduced forms). For real case bnfisprincipal may provide solution heuristically subexponential in D assuming GRH. Library: GEN qfbsolve(GEN Q, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadclassunit
rubrics_metrics.description: Buchmann–McCurley sub-exponential algorithm for computing class group of quadratic order of discriminant D. Should be used instead of qfbclassno or quadregulator when D<-10^25, D>10^10, or when structure wanted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is vector v with members: v.no (class number), v.cyc (structure as product of cyclic groups), v.gen (generators as binary quadratic forms), v.reg (regulator computed to internal accuracy or default). flag is obsolete. tech parameter [c1,c2] controls execution time and stack size and balances relation finding and linear algebra; default chosen to be provably correct under GRH. Library: GEN quadclassunit0(GEN D, long flag, GEN tech = NULL, long prec). For experimenting use GEN Buchquad(GEN D, double c1, double c2, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quaddisc
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of quadratic field Q(sqrt(x)) where x ∈ Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN quaddisc(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadgen
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates quadratic number ω = (a + sqrt(D))/2 where a=0 if D≡0 mod4, a=1 if D≡1 mod4 so that (1,ω) is integral basis for quadratic order of discriminant D. D must be integer congruent 0 or1 mod4, not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN quadgen(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadhilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation defining Hilbert class field of quadratic field of discriminant D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If D<0 uses complex multiplication (Schertz variant). If D>0 uses Stark units and may return vector of extensions whose compositum is requested class field. See bnrstark for details. Library: GEN quadhilbert(GEN D, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates canonical quadratic polynomial (in variable v) corresponding to discriminant D, i.e. minimal polynomial of quadgen(D). D must be integer ≡ 0 or 1 mod4 and not a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN quadpoly0(GEN D, long v = -1) where v is variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadray
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation for ray class field of conductor f for quadratic field of discriminant D using analytic methods. Accepts bnf for x^2 - D in place of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For D<0 uses σ function and Schertz method. For D>0 uses Stark's conjecture and may return vector of relative equations. See bnrstark for details. Library: GEN quadray(GEN D, GEN f, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadregulator
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulator of quadratic field of positive discriminant x. Returns error if x not a discriminant or if x is a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See quadclassunit if x large. Library: GEN quadregulator(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadunit
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental unit of real quadratic field Q(sqrt(D)) where D is discriminant of the field. If D not fundamental discriminant probably gives fundamental unit of corresponding order. D must be integer ≡0 or1 mod4, not a square; result is quadratic number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN quadunit(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: randomprime
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a strong pseudoprime in [2, N-1] (default N=2^31). If N is vector [a,b] returns pseudoprime a ≤ p ≤ b. If no prime exists in interval function may loop infinitely. If upper bound < 2^64 returned pseudoprime is proven prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN randomprime(GEN N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: removeprimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes primes listed in x from prime number table. If x omitted lists current extra primes. Passing addprimes() then removeprimes(addprimes()) empties extra prime table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x can be single integer or vector. Library: GEN removeprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: sigma / sumdivk
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of kth powers of positive divisors of |x|. x and k must be integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN sumdivk(GEN x, long k). Also GEN sumdiv(GEN n) for k=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtint
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer square root of x: largest integer y such that y^2 ≤ x for non-negative integer x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows difference between sqrtint and floating sqrt. Library: GEN sqrtint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtnint
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer n-th root of x: largest integer y such that y^n ≤ x for non-negative integer x. Special case n=2 is sqrtint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN sqrtnint(GEN x, long n). Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: stirling
rubrics_metrics.description: Stirling numbers: s(n,k) of first kind (flag=1 default) or S(n,k) of second kind (flag=2), with n,k non-negative integers. First kind is (−1)^{n−k} times number of permutations of n symbols with k cycles; second kind counts partitions of n elements into k non-empty subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all s(n,k) are needed it's faster to compute coefficients of x(x−1)...(x−n+1) and extract coefficients. Library: GEN stirling(n,k,{flag=1}).
